title: War—What Is It Good For?

War—What Is It Good For?

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 24 Nov 2026

In too many reports to list, I have quoted the words of wisdom imparted to me very early in my career by Gavekal’s very first client, the late Beat Notz of Notz Stucki in Geneva. Beat once took me aside and said “Remember, Louis, that when things in the market become very challenging, the German Bundesbank will always do what it can to save the bondholders, while US policymakers will bend over backwards to save the equity holders. So when in doubt, when the markets are in turmoil, when things get tough, then just buy German bunds and US stocks. Over the very long term, it always works”.Of course, in the years that followed these words of advice, the Bundesbank was murdered by the European Central Bank and its role taken up by the People’s Bank of China (see my 2019 book Clash of Empires: Currencies and Power in a Multipolar World). This has left Chinese government bonds as the only credible “store of value” bond market.
